title: Hunter Education Commission
definition: The Hunter Education Commission, officially known as the Indian Education Commission (1882-83), was appointed by Viceroy Lord Ripon to review the implementation of Wood's Despatch of 1854 and assess the state of primary and secondary education in British India.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for Modern Indian History (GS-1). Frequently tested in Prelims regarding chronology, specific recommendations (mass primary education, private enterprise), and often confused with the Hunter Committee of 1919 (Jallianwala Bagh).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts, objectives, and historical context of the Hunter Commission.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions regarding primary vs. secondary education.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions without confusing it with the 1919 Hunter Committee.
prerequisites: Evolution of British educational policy in India
